subject: Temporary deletion/retention exemption request for debugging — AcmeTech
messages:
From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acmesech.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: product-ops@acmesech.com
Date: 2026-02-20T08:15:00-08:00
Subject: Investigating redaction failures — request for temporary retention of trace logs

Hi Lauren,

We're seeing intermittent redaction failures in our production traffic that appear to be correlated with requests routed through your EU region endpoints. To investigate we need access to raw request/response traces for a small set of request IDs — specifically the last 48 hours plus any reproductions. Our retention policy normally deletes raw payloads quickly, so we are asking Redwood if you can temporarily make an exception for AcmeTech (EU data residency) to retain those traces for debugging.

Key constraints from our side:
- Data must remain in EU-hosted storage and not be exported outside the region.
- Access should be limited and auditable.
- We are willing to sign an NDA or addendum if required.

If possible we'd like a short window (48–72 hours) to let our SREs and your engineers reproduce and confirm fixes. Please let me know what information you need from us (request IDs, timestamps, sample payloads) and the steps/redlines for an exception. This is impacting a small subset of users but it's a blocker for our release next week, so timely help would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Sarah Connors
Sr. SRE, AcmeTech
product-ops@acmesech.com
+44 20 5555 0101

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acmesech.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-20T09:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Investigating redaction failures — request for temporary retention of trace logs

Hi Sarah — thanks for the heads up and sorry you're seeing this.

Short answer: we can support a time-limited, auditable retention exception for debugging purposes provided a few controls are in place. We cannot change the data residency — any exception must keep data stored and accessed only within the EU cluster.

What we need to proceed:
- A ticket (I created JIRA INF-3421) — please add the list of request IDs and sample timestamps in that ticket.
- Signed retention override form (attached: retention-override-form.pdf).
- Confirmation that Acme will not request exports outside the EU during the window.
- Your preferred retention window (we recommend 7 days where possible to give time for reproduction & verification).

Operational notes:
- Access will be restricted to named engineers and logged centrally.
- We will provide an audit log and deletion verification after the window closes.
- Engineering needs the request IDs and any reproducer payloads to scope the work.

Cc'ing Dev (infra) and Vivek (security) to confirm the technical feasibility and to approve the exception. Once we have the signed form and the ticket updated, Dev — can you estimate turnaround and any safeguards we should require? Vivek — would you please confirm any additional compliance constraints?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acmesech.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-20T11:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Investigating redaction failures — request for temporary retention of trace logs

Thanks Lauren / Sarah — I can take this.

Technical plan (high level):
- We will enable a temporary "debug retention override" flag scoped to AcmeTech's tenant in the EU cluster. That will keep raw traces (request/response + kv-cache) for the requested request IDs.
- Access will be via a short-lived role bound to up to 3 engineers (two from our side + one from Acme if you prefer) and all access will be logged to the central audit stream.
- We'll run an automated scrub on non-required PII fields where feasible and will provide the redaction_playbook.pdf to show what is redacted versus preserved.
- Once the window closes, we will run a deletion verification job and store a signed deletion log in the ticket.

Turnaround: if Vivek signs off and we have the signed form + request IDs, we can apply the override within ~2 hours during business hours. If you can attach the sample request IDs to INF-3421 now, I'll queue the job.

Please include the exact request IDs + sample timestamps (ISO8601) and specify if you want us to allow an Acme engineer to be included in the access group.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
dev.patel@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acmesech.com>
Date: 2026-02-21T11:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Investigating redaction failures — request for temporary retention of trace logs (APPROVED, controls listed)

I'm approving a time-limited retention exception for AcmeTech under the following mandatory constraints: 

1) Window: 7-day maximum starting at the time the override is enabled.
2) Residency: Data must remain in the EU cluster. No export or cross-region sync permitted.
3) Access: Maximum of 3 named engineers (list to be provided in INF-3421). Access requires MFA and will be time-bound.
4) Auditing: All reads/writes will be captured and attached to the JIRA ticket. We will provide a deletion verification artifact (signed) after day 7.
5) Redaction: Apply the redaction playbook first where it doesn't impede debugging; if full raw payloads are required, document rationale in the ticket.
6) Legal: Acme must sign the retention-override-form.pdf. No further export or retention beyond the approved window without a fresh approval.

Attaching our internal checklist (temporary-retention-checklist.pdf) to confirm the above items have been completed before enablement. Dev — proceed to schedule the override once INF-3421 contains the request IDs and the signed form is uploaded.

Sarah — once we run deletion verification I'll email the signed verification log and a summary of access events. If Acme needs a named Red Team engineer present during testing, include that person in the JIRA comment.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security & Compliance (interim)
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
